what_was_verified: The supporting public repository exposes multiple ASKAP J1832 dynamic-spectrum pickle files spanning approximately 1.3 MB to tens of MB.
The authors provide vis_ds.py and burst.py for loading/folding dynamic spectra and notebooks for the discovery plot, folded polarization, and simultaneous wide-frequency analysis.
The authors point to primary ASKAP, GMRT and MeerKAT archives for raw data.
The current connected GitHub path exposes repository metadata/text but does not provide a trusted non-executable numeric conversion path inside this pass.
why_this_is_a_training_success: TOPA learned that eagerness to inspect an interesting target is itself a source of methodological risk. A blocked gate with preserved provenance is preferable to unsafe execution or a visual-only morphology claim mislabeled as numeric replay.
allowed_next_routes: retrieve author-exported safe numeric array or trusted Zenodo representation
retrieve primary-archive raw telescope product and rebuild the dynamic spectrum independently
materialize pickle bytes in an isolated environment and audit pickle opcodes/globals before any conversion, without importing arbitrary globals
use rendered products only as calibration and keep them explicitly separate from numeric replay
